beliefs: The outer branch is odd: f(-x) = -f(x) for |x|>=2, i.e. f(x) = sign(x)*|f(|x|)|, with NEGATIVE values for x>0 and POSITIVE for x<0 [E1, E8, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21]
On the positive outer branch |f(x)| follows a smooth log-linear law ln|f| = lnA + p*ln|x| + k*|x| fit to the full positive-side data [E7, E10, E15, E17, E19, E20]
On the negative outer branch |f(x)| follows a separate smooth log-linear law ln|f| = lnA' + p'*ln|x| + k'*|x| fit to the negative-side data [E8, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21]
Negative-side outer magnitudes exceed positive-side by a factor decaying from ~2.3 at |x|=2.1 to ~1 at |x|>=48, then ~1.03 at large |x| [E10, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21]
f(2)=-60.2 and f(-2)=-67.0; the outer law is continuous through |x|=2 on both sides [E1, E4, E6, E19]
On (0,1) f is exactly 0, with a sharp step to -4.3 at x=1.0 [E5, E9]
On (1,2) f rises smoothly from -4.3 toward ~-30 as x->2- [E3, E4, E5, E9, E19]
On (-2,0) f is a smooth curve: ~+6 near -1, peaking ~+8 near -1.2, then dropping steeply to -67 at x=-2 [E3, E6]
There is a genuine jump discontinuity at x=2 on the positive side (from ~-30 at x->2- to -60.2 at x=2) [E19]
notes: Fixed the sign convention: outer branch is odd with f(x)=sign(x)*|f(|x|)| (negative for x>0, positive for x<0), which E8/E14/E16/E18/E20/E21 all confirm. Replaced the negative-side ratio table with a separate log-linear fit to negative-side data so it generalizes to unsampled points.
